stage1.impression: A globe of overlapping translucent discs with a bright pinwheel at its centre. The 3D read is real, and the lockup with the heavy EARF wordmark is well proportioned. But the overlaps mix toward olive and khaki, and on night the dark-green body sinks into the ground, so at lockup size (about 80 px) it reads as a murky, busy ball. The one-colour rails lose the acrylic idea entirely: they fall back to lumpy thick-thin rings almost identical to the 'even' style, an open wireframe rather than the filled ball, so the mark changes character between rails. Nobody could draw it from memory. The ident has a logical story (spin, tilt into pose, hold, slide aside, wordmark) but plays stop-start. The spin decays to nothing by about 0.8 s and there is a dead stop around 1.18-1.53 s. The energy peaks on a stock slide aside and a jagged hard wipe (1.93-2.15 s) that starts while the globe is still crowding the E (frame 07), and it ends on a 1.4 s dead freeze. A competent draft: muddy in colour, generic in motion.

keep: The pinwheel: at the centre, the blue equator crossing the orange and violet meridian halves makes a four-way wedge figure, the one detail people will remember. It reads at lockup size (sheet 2, frames 08-12) and in both the discs and the acrylic; every change below is built to keep it legible.

The gyro landing into the 23.4° lean (sheet 2, frames 01-05): a turn about an upright axis that tips into Earth's tilt and lands exactly on the canonical pose. It is the one move that could only be this brand; change 2 makes it the spine of the ident instead of a prelude.

changes.problem: The acrylic does not read as a transparent version of the discs: the ground takes a share of every point inside the ball and the green is mixed into every disc in front of it, so the body turns sage on paper and dark olive on night, every colour drifts toward green, and back halves show as olive patches.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, same points in the discs and the acrylic: body #7B9E6A on paper and #416732 on ink against the discs' #4F7F3A (OKLab ΔE 0.118 and 0.077); top of the red oval, a back half seen through the green, #828011 / #6A7705 (olive) where the discs show green; blue band #3A98BD / #2F8AB6 against #4A90C8; yellow front half #CDAE38 against #E9B320. Rebuilt from the card's rule, the render matches the published panels on 98.8% of pixels: 40% of the ball differs from the discs by more than 0.05, with about 44 flat colours to the discs' 6. Sheet 2, frames 08-12: at about 80 px in the lockup the globe reads murky beside the white wordmark.
changes.parameter: acrylic layering inside the ball (new rule)
changes.from: every disc crossed, the green included, keeps face of what shows, front to back; the ground takes what is left
changes.to: Inside the ball the ground takes nothing and the green (the meridian facing the viewer, with its fill) is the backing. Where one or more of the five coloured discs lie in front of the green, they share all of what shows: the nearest keeps face, the next face of the rest, and the farthest coloured disc takes what is left; the green takes nothing there. Where no coloured disc lies in front of the green, the green keeps all of what shows. Colours mixed in OKLCh as now; outside the ball unchanged.
changes.expected: Sheet 3: the acrylic's body is the discs' own green #4F7F3A on paper and on ink, and every area where one disc shows is that disc's flat colour from the discs (blue #4A90C8, red #D2382F, yellow #E9B320, orange #E5732A, violet #6C4BA3). New colours appear only where two coloured discs cross: vermilion, crimson, cornflower, indigo, amber, plum. There is no sage rim on paper and no dark-olive body on night. The share of the ball more than 0.05 from the discs falls from 40% to about 10%, and the flat colours from about 44 to about 18. In the lockup (sheet 2, frames 08-12) the globe is as bright as the discs.

accept.check: Is the acrylic's green at the left edge of the ball the same green as the discs' beside it, on paper and on ink, and is the blue band's outer end the same blue as the discs'?

changes.problem: The ident plays stop-start: the half-turn is spent early and creeps, the tilt is a 0.2 s blip, the globe then stands dead before a stock slide aside, and the end freezes for 1.47 s; two-thirds of the frame steps are under the still line, and the brand's own move carries the least energy.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, frames 01-03 (0.00-0.67 s): a 180° turn, 126° of it done by 0.33 s and 174° by 0.67 s (fitted against the model). The trace falls from 0.0074 at 0.07 s to under 0.2% at 0.43 s and creeps there until 0.83 s; the tilt bump peaks at only 0.005 (0.80-1.00 s). It is flat from 1.00 to 1.57 s (0.567 s, 'spun'/'whole'), peaks at 0.015-0.020 for the aside and wipe (1.55-2.13 s), and is flat again from 2.17 to 3.63 s (1.47 s; frames 09-12 identical). 67% of frame steps are under 0.2%.
changes.parameter: globe timeline (spin, tilt, spun, whole, aside, EARF marks)
changes.expected: The trace is one continuous decay from the spin, through the tilt, into a single smoother aside hump (peak about 0.013, was 0.0197), then the wordmark. Nothing is flat until about 2.57 s, and the still end card lasts about 1.07 s (was 1.47 s). Frames 04-06 show the globe still turning as it leans in and starts to travel. Frame 07 (1.97 s) shows it halfway, still turning, with no letters yet. It comes to rest in exactly the canonical pose at its lockup place at 2.32 s. In simulation the longest still before 2.3 s falls from 0.567 s to 0.03 s. A 360° turn is not enough: its slow tail drops under the still line for about 0.27 s.

changes.problem: Where two coloured sheets cross, the mix keeps their average lightness, so crossings come out paler or pastel instead of deeper. That is the opposite of stacked tinted acrylic, and it falls short of the owner's 'push it further'.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, acrylic on paper, pinwheel: the lower-left wedge, where the blue band crosses the orange lens, and the top wedge, where red crosses violet, barely separate from their front colours. At face 0.72 the crossings sit 0.025-0.10 (OKLab) from the front disc, orange over blue only 0.025, and no crossing is darker than the darker of its two sheets. Lowering face instead turns them lavender and orchid: blue over orange becomes #8C80D8 at 0.65.
changes.parameter: stack_darkening: OKLab L subtracted at a crossing for each coloured disc beyond the first lying in front of the green
changes.expected: Each crossing becomes a deeper version of the colours that meet there: crimson #B42649 where red lies over violet, plum #863588 where violet lies over red, deep cornflower #5C7FCC in the lower-left pinwheel wedge, burnt orange #D35619 where orange lies over red, amber #DE9400 where yellow lies over orange. The front colour still names each crossing. The back halves seen through the green are not darkened, and at lockup size the globe stays as bright as the discs.

accept.at: sheet 3, acrylic on paper and on ink
accept.check: Do the crossings read as deeper, richer versions of the colours that meet there (deep crimson where red meets violet, deep amber where yellow meets orange) rather than paler or pastel ones?

changes.problem: Once the ground no longer shows inside the ball, the separate ink value only makes the crossings weaker on night than on paper, so the same mark would differ by ground.
changes.evidence: Card: face 0.72 on paper, 0.80 on ink. Sheet 3: r2's acrylic on paper and on ink differ visibly (body #7B9E6A against #416732; olive patch #828011 against #6A7705). Sheet 2 is on night, so the ident shows the weaker ink crossings.
changes.expected: Inside the rim, the acrylic on ink matches the acrylic on paper region for region, with the same crossing colours. The crossings in the night ident are as visible as on paper.

accept.at: sheet 3, acrylic on paper vs acrylic on ink
accept.check: Inside the rim, is the acrylic on ink identical, region for region, to the acrylic on paper?

changes.problem: Under the new rule the back halves vanish, and with them the cue that most says 'transparent'. In r2 they show, but as olive patches through a washed green.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3: top of the red oval is #828011 on paper and #6A7705 on ink, where the discs show green #4F7F3A. It is the back half of the red disc seen through 0.72 green plus 0.08 paper, about 0.07 from the green: strong enough to read as a new olive shape.
changes.parameter: face_green: share the green keeps where it lies in front of coloured back halves (they share the rest: nearest face of it, farthest the remainder)
changes.expected: In the large views, the back halves of the red, yellow and orange discs show as faint shapes in the green (about #5F7D24, #5F8536 and #60812D against #4F7F3A, ΔE 0.02-0.03); the blue and violet ones barely show. No area reads olive, and at lockup size (frames 08-12) the globe looks the same as with them hidden.

accept.check: Inside the top of the red oval, can you just make out the back half of the red disc as a faint shape in the green, without it reading as an olive patch?

changes.problem: The wordmark arrives by a constant-speed hard wipe that slices letters and, in r2, runs while the globe is still travelling. It is a mechanical, generic move after a gesture that otherwise decelerates into rest.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, frame 07 (t = 1.97 s): the E is complete and the A is cut by a vertical edge, while the globe is still 8 px right of and 3 px larger than its lockup place, half the final gap from the E. The trace from 1.90 to 2.13 s saws 0.019 / 0.016 / 0.020 / 0.010 / 0.012 / 0.002 / 0.007, the sharpest peak in the ident (0.0197 at 1.97 s).
changes.expected: The letters come on after the globe has landed: quick at first, slowing into the F, finished at 2.60 s. The wordmark section of the trace is one lower hump (about 0.012 at most in simulation, against about 0.014 for the linear wipe at the new time). Frame 08 (2.30 s) shows the globe at rest with at most a sliver of the E; frame 09 (2.63 s) shows the full lockup.

most_important: Change 1. Make the green the ball's backing and take the ground out of the ball, so every single-disc area keeps the discs' own flat colour on paper and on ink, and only crossings of coloured discs mix. This one rule answers the owner's round-25 complaint ('a transparent version of the discs, but it looks very different'), clears the olive and sage, and makes the night ident and the lockup bright again.
out_of_scope: One-colour rails (black only, white only, a speaker's own): the acrylic becomes the lines, as the owner asked ('The strokes should be the non-color versions'), and the lines style is fixed. In sheet 1 (rows 2-3, black only), though, those lines pool into lumpy blobs where several thick-thin bands stack at the silhouette (lower left, upper right). As an open wireframe they also lose the filled ball's silhouette, so the mark changes character between rails. Recognition across rails depends on fixing this, in the lines style.

Discs style (fixed): the black-only and white-only discs (sheet 1, row 1, cells 1-2) carry stray hooks and broken fragments along the bottom of the rim. They will show in print and at small sizes, and since the acrylic is defined as these discs, the defects travel with it.

Geometry and colours (fixed): six discs at three angles can be recognised but not drawn from memory; what people will keep is 'a ball with a pinwheel'. That caps how far any style can go on the draw-from-memory test, and it also decides which colours cross (see for_owner).
for_owner: Primaries never cross primaries in this geometry. In front of the green, the red, yellow and blue parallels never overlap one another. The only place they overlap in the view is a thin sliver where the front of the red oval passes over the back of the blue band, which sits behind the green. Every crossing pairs a parallel with a side meridian, so the mixes are vermilion, crimson, plum, cornflower, indigo, amber and ochre, never green from blue and yellow. Literal 'primaries make secondaries' would need the colours reassigned (for example primaries on the meridians). The colours are fixed, so that is yours to decide.

How see-through: change 5 lets the back halves show at 10% through the green. That is the cue that most says 'transparent', but it adds faint shapes the discs don't have. Set it to 1.0 for none (the acrylic then differs from the discs only at crossings), or about 0.85 for more (above that strength they start to read olive again).

A single-colour acrylic for 'a speaker's own' colour: one tint, each extra sheet a step deeper. It would carry the acrylic idea, and the tinted cabinet, into one colour. Your round-24b rule says non-colour versions are strokes; decide whether 'single color' counts as non-colour.

Polished edges: real cast acrylic glows at its edges, and a hairline lighter edge (about 0.01 of the radius, the disc's own tint 0.1 lighter) would say so. It is a kind of stroke, which you ruled out for the discs in round 24b, so it is not prescribed unless you want it.

End card: the retiming keeps the 3.65 s length and ends on a still lockup of about 1.07 s. Say so if broadcast or retail needs a longer still end card; otherwise the globe could keep a slow turn through the hold and land on the canonical pose at the end.
